site.name: Horsfal Mine
site.location: Gold Run, about one mile east of Gold Hill
site.componentDetail: Historic Horsfal gold lode and underground mine on Gold Run east of Gold Hill, discovered in 1859 and central to the district's earliest hard-rock mining and milling.
overview: The Horsfal Mine was one of the earliest productive hard-rock gold mines in the Gold Hill district. David Horsfal, William Blore, and M. L. McCaslin discovered the lode in 1859 soon after the placer rush began along Gold Run.

Rich Horsfal ore helped sustain Gold Hill and encouraged early milling experiments. A July 1860 stamp-mill operation reportedly recovered hundreds of dollars of gold from each cord of ore, demonstrating that the district's lodes could reward improved processing.

timeline.text: David Horsfal, William Blore, and M. L. McCaslin discovered the Horsfal Lode after the first placer and fissure claims at Gold Hill.
Ore from the Horsfal helped support one of Boulder County's earliest successful stamp-mill operations, which began running near Gold Hill in July.
The mine operated through Gold Hill's first boom; later historical accounts credited the Horsfal with roughly $200,000 in early gold production.
Historic photographs preserved by the Carnegie Library document the Horsfal Mine and its mine buildings near Gold Hill.
The Horsfal, Black Cloud, and Slide mines were consolidated under Slide Mines, Inc.; the combined operation became a major Boulder County gold enterprise.

moreHistory: Boulder County's historic survey places the Horsfal discovery within the creation of Mining District No. 1 of Nebraska Territory, an early miners' government organized before Colorado Territory existed.
A contemporary county history described the Horsfal as a rich and famous find and recorded recovery of as much as $600 to $700 per cord from selected ore during the early milling period.

The mapped point is a historic mine-site reference, not a safe entrance or an assurance of public access. Mine workings may be unstable, and visitors should remain on lawful public routes and never enter openings.
